title: Purge Harmonization Service: deterministic deletion workflows and tamper-evident audit export
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a production-ready Purge Harmonization Service (PHS) that unifies tenant-scoped deletion across data planes (primary DB rows, object storage, blob backups, KV caches, and derived analytics), provides deterministic deletion workflows, and emits tamper-evident audit bundles customers can fetch and verify.

Scope:
- API: synchronous for small scopes (<100k objects) and asynchronous long-running jobs for large scopes.
- Audit bundle: cryptographically chained deletion manifest (SHA256 chain) with KMS-signed root hash, region stamping, start/end timestamps, and per-resource final status.
- Console UX: tenant-delete flow with preview, retention overlap warnings, legal-hold detection, and a downloadable receipt.
- Operator tooling: purge simulator, retry-safe erase workers, and a queue for cross-region dependency resolution.
- Exports: support JSONL and compressed tarball for large bundles, plus a verification API to confirm a receipt against our public verification endpoint.

Non-goals:
- Not implementing an immutable public blockchain; audit bundles are internally generated and signed using customer-specific KMS keys for enterprises.
- Not covering third-party downstream data copies (we will document expectations and provide connectors where possible).

Design decisions:
1) Deterministic deletion plan: compute a canonical list of affected keys/objects at request time and store an immutable plan to ensure idempotence and reproducibility. This allows deterministic replays for investigation or dispute.
2) Tamper-evident bundles: chain each deletion event hash into a manifest; sign the manifest root with either Redwood KMS or customer-managed KMS when in Private mode.
3) Tenant-scoped vs global retention: enforce tenant-scoped deletes preferentially; global retention sweeps use the same engine but different authorization and SLA.
4) Verification API: provide GET /deletions/{id}/audit-bundle and POST /deletions/verify which allows customers to submit a receipt or bundle hash and receive signed verification.

Acceptance criteria:
- API to create deletion requests and return job id; small-scope synchronous deletes complete with status=done within SLA (target: 60s median for <=10k items).
- Audit bundle generated for every completed deletion with root hash signature present.
- Console shows preview count and byte-size estimate; prevents deletion if legal hold is detected with clear operator guidance.
- E2E tests that verify replay of deletion plan results in no-op on second run and that manifest signatures verify against KMS public key.
- Telemetry: per-tenant deletion latency histogram, failure reasons breakdown, bytes removed by storage class, and audit bundle delivery success.

API contract (summary):
- POST /v1/deletions (body: tenant_id, scope: {filters}, request_mode: sync|async, retention_policy_override: optional, reason: string) => 202 with job_id or 200 with result for sync.
- GET /v1/deletions/{job_id}/status => status, progress, estimated_completion, affected_counts.
- GET /v1/deletions/{job_id}/audit-bundle => signed manifest (JSONL) or 404 if not ready.
- POST /v1/deletions/verify (body: receipt_hash, signature) => verification_result {valid: true|false, details}.

Operational considerations:
- Workers must be idempotent: each resource deletion is recorded with final state and timestamp so retries are safe.
- Cross-region object references: use dependent-delete graph to ensure child objects are removed before parents where necessary.
- Legal hold: if object has an active legal hold label, deletion must be blocked and operator notified; allow a privileged override only with audit trail.
- Data residency: deletion operations must run in the data's residency region; audit manifests include region tag and proof-of-execution region ID.

Telemetry & SLOs:
- Deletion job success rate >= 99.5% for P0 tenants within SLA.
- Audit bundle generation success >= 99%.
- Console preview accuracy within ±5% for item counts.

Rollout plan:
1) Dev: implement core engine and local KMS signing; unit tests and integration tests with synthetic tenants. (2 sprints).
2) Canary: enable for internal customers and a small cohort of opt-in customers; collect telemetry and edge cases. (1 sprint).
3) Gradual rollout by tenant size; enable customer-managed KMS option for private deployments in rollout phase 2. (2 sprints).
4) GA: public docs, SDK examples, and compliance whitepaper.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: accidental over-deletion due to filter mismatch. Mitigation: preview + change-proof confirmation + dry-run mode + explicit per-tenant manifest.
- Risk: audit bundle forgery. Mitigation: KMS-signed manifests and publishable verification endpoints.
- Risk: long-running deletes cause resource contention. Mitigation: priority queueing, rate-limited workers, and dedicated reserved capacity for large purges.

Acceptance tests and QA checklist:
- dry-run produces deterministic plan matching actual run
- re-run of same job_id is idempotent (no additional deletions)
- manifest verification works for both Redwood-signed and customer-KMS-signed manifests
- console flow blocks when legal hold exists and surfaces remediation steps
- retention edge-cases: overlapping retention windows and TTL+manual delete combinations

Docs & artifacts:
- Confluence: /spaces/PD/pages/PHS-design (draft)
- Design spec: link to Drive (design/PHS-manifest-v1.md)
- Prototype PR: github.com/redwood-inference/purge-engine/pull/274 (WIP)

Next steps (this ticket):
- Finalize API surface and write request/response schemas.
- Wire up KMS signing prototype and store verification keys in keystore.
- Implement console preview and dry-run state.
- Coordinate with ENG on worker capacity and scheduling knobs.

Metrics for success after GA:
- Reduction in manual compliance tickets by 80% for deletion/evidence requests.
- 95% of customer verification requests return verifiable receipts without human intervention.
- Customer satisfaction for deletion flows >= 4.5/5 in follow-up survey for early adopters.
